rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4 <U+2014> the authors process 8 PlanetScope surface-reflectance images of the Araguaia River (Jan-Jul 2018), compute NDVI-based flooded areas in four buffers and regress them against in-situ gauge and JASON-2 data (Tables 1-2, Fig. 5). Q2: Section 4 and Eqs. 2-4 <U+2014> flooded area in the 500 m buffer predicts river flow (R2 = 96.49%), water level (R2 = 94.38%) and altimetry (R2 = 88.83%); abstract states CubeSat images can serve as a CubeSat Virtual Station to estimate river flow and height variation. Q3: Sections 3.2 and 4 <U+2014> the CubeSat-derived estimates are checked against two independent references, the in-situ Conventional Station (gauge discharge and level) and the JASON-2 satellite altimetry virtual station. Q4: Section 3.2 step 3-4 and Table 2 <U+2014> the mechanism (discharge changes water level, which changes inundated surface area) is measured: NDVI-classified water area per buffer and CS water level, with the level-flow rating (Fig. 4a, R2 = 1) and level-area relationship (Eq. 3) reported. Q7: Discussion <U+2014> authors state that a buffer of 0.5 to 1 times the average river width is needed to reach a high and stable R2, and that only complete-coverage, cloud-free surface-reflectance images were usable (Table 1, 14 of 22 dates discarded). Q8: Discussion <U+2014> only 8 images used; CVS less accurate at higher discharges when the level rises inside the channel without expanding the flooded area; precision depends on channel-edge slope; the authors call it a proof of concept predicting flow at a monthly scale. Q9: Table 3 <U+2014> standard deviation of the estimation errors reported as precision estimator (553.63 m3/s for flow, 37.16 cm for level, 0.34 m for altimetry) alongside RMSE.
rows.notes: The core of the passage (accurate river flow and height estimation from CubeSat images at a CVS) is directly tested. The downstream part of the passage (sub-basin monitoring for efficient water management, especially in developing countries) is a recommendation/conclusion, not a tested outcome. Q5: single river reach in one biome, so no. Q6: result is for one 500 m-buffer virtual station on the Araguaia River; although river discharge integrates the sub-basin, the study does not demonstrate monitoring across a sub-basin or multiple stations, and the sub-basin/continental application is stated as future work, so no (some doubt). Q3: both references are validation data for the same CubeSat method, but they are independent measurement systems (ground gauge and satellite altimetry); counted as yes. Q9: the reported SD is the dispersion of the residuals, which is close in kind to RMSE; counted as yes because a standard deviation is explicitly reported.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a single-site, single-season (Jan-Jul 2018, 8 images) proof-of-concept on the Araguaia River, Brazil.
